scenes.title: AWS Textract: From Scanned Invoice to Structured Data
scenes.narration: The final slide traces a scanned supplier invoice through document extraction and normalisation. Begin with the PDF or image: vendor name, invoice number, date, billing address and line-item table are visible on the page. Textract DetectDocumentText extracts detected text blocks, while AnalyzeDocument with appropriate features can identify forms and tables. For a specialised expense document, an expense-oriented API can return invoice fields in a more directly usable representation. The middle panel shows extracted values and confidence scores; those are estimates of extraction certainty, not approval of the invoice's financial accuracy. The application then normalises them into a structured record with fields for vendor, number, date, buyer and line items. Keep page references, bounding boxes and confidence for audit and correction. Check arithmetic and field associations: a detected total, tax and subtotal should be validated against line items instead of silently accepted. Sensitive financial documents should have controlled S3 storage, encryption and scoped IAM permissions. The value of Textract is turning unstructured document pixels into machine-readable information that downstream systems can verify and process.
